title: Enhancement: Support new BIOS on NH-4010 and NH-4020
author: louis-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the enhancement

Support new BIOS on Nexthop's NH-4010 and NH-4020

### Current Behavior

New BIOS has moved PCIe addresses of some PCIe devices and has shut off some non-critical PCIe devices.

### Proposed Behavior

1. We cannot use hard-coded PCIe addresses to refer to the devices anymore. The PCIe address of each device must be determined after boot in a deterministic way.
2. Update `pcie.yaml` with dynamic PCIe addresses, so that `sudo show platform pcie --check` will still pass on the new BIOS.

#### Why I did it

Fixes #24059

Add support for new BIOS on these platforms:
- x86_64-nexthop_4010-r0
- x86_64-nexthop_4010-r1
- x86_64-nexthop_4020-r0

New BIOS (e.g. `Komodo-nosb-7.2`) has moved PCIe addresses of some PCIe devices and has shut off some non-critical PCIe devices.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

1. Converted these files into jinja2 template: `pddf-device.json` -> `pddf-device.json.j2` and `pcie.yaml` -> `pcie.yaml.j2`, so that we can assign PCIe addresses to them after boot.
2. Create `pcie-variables.yaml` to help lookup the PCIe addresses/buses. Note that we look up the bus from device's associated PCIe root port which is always deterministic.
3. Create `nh_gen` CLI to generate `pddf-device.json` and `pcie.yaml` at runtime. It gets the list of variables from `pcie-variables.yaml` and feed into the according Jinja2 template file to produce the output.
4. Refactor `asic_init.sh` and `system_powercycle` scripts into common ones (that are shared across both NH-4010 and NH-4020) and get PCIe addresses dynamically.
    - We also apply the latest technique in asic_init.sh so it works best with the new BIOS to avoid unexpected reboot
    - We also trigger `asic_init.sh` when syncd restarts (which the script will know it is in "asic reset" mode)
5. Update `rename_mgmt_interface.sh` to use dynamic PCIe addreses.

Note that these changes are backward compatible with DUT on old BIOS.

#### How to verify it

- `sudo show platform pcie --check` PASSED.
- DUT can boot and `show platform` commands give expected output.

comments.body:
> It's not a good way to touch the common opennsl switch driver load sequence in your platform asic initial script. You can consider to have platform init service and make the ordering in the system service file.

Thanks for the suggestion! I've updated to use the systemd ordering. Note that I didn't create a new platform init service, but just make sure `pddf-platform-init.service` finish before starting `opennsl-modules.service`. As I believe the pddf init doesn't rely on ASIC being initialized.
